prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1240; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to talk with me today. This recorded statement is for our claim file. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, but you can use the claim number.
Q: That works. Can you describe where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was driving on a two-lane road in Houston, heading toward the highway entrance. It was late afternoon and traffic was moving slowly.
Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: The car in front of me stopped suddenly, so I slowed down. Then a vehicle coming the other way drifted over into my lane.
Q: How fast were you traveling?
A: Maybe fifteen or twenty miles an hour. It wasn't fast at all.
Q: Did you try to avoid the other vehicle?
A: Yes, I braked and turned the wheel to the right, but there wasn't much room. We clipped each other head-on, more of a glancing hit than a full crash.
Q: Did the airbags deploy in your vehicle?
A: No, they didn't. I just felt a hard jolt and my seatbelt locked up.
Q: Were you injured, and if so, where?
A: My left wrist hit the steering wheel. It swelled up right away, and the doctor said it's fractured. I've got a cast on it now and I can't use my hand much.
Q: Did you seek medical treatment at the scene or afterward?
A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room that night, and I've been seeing an orthopedic doctor since.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Just that I was driving carefully and I'd like this claim handled quickly, since I'm missing work.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
